title: Disease-Associated Non-Coding Variants Alter NKX2-5 DNA-Binding Affinity
authors: Edwin G. Peña-Martínez; Alejandro Rivera-Madera; Diego A. Pomales-Matos; Leandro Sanabria-Alberto; Brittany M. Rosario-Cañuelas; Jessica M. Rodríguez-Ríos; Emmanuel A. Carrasquillo-Dones; José A. Rodríguez-Martínez
one_liner_zh: 该文用PWM预测并EMSA验证非编码SNP对NKX2-5 TF-DNA结合亲和力的影响，聚焦TF-DNA互作但方法为传统PWM与湿实验，缺乏AI或物理模拟建模，故为中档匹配。
abstract: 1. Abstract Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have mapped over 90% of disease- or trait-associated variants within the non-coding genome, like cis -regulatory elements (CREs). Non-coding single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) are genomic variants that can change how DNA-binding regulatory proteins, like transcription factors (TFs), interact with the genome and regulate gene expression. NKX2-5 is a TF essential for proper heart development, and mutations affecting its function have been associated with congenital heart diseases (CHDs). However, establishing a causal mechanism between non-coding genomic variants and human disease remains challenging. To address this challenge, we identified 8,475 SNPs predicted to alter NKX2-5 DNA- binding using a position weight matrix (PWM)-based predictive model. Five variants were prioritized for in vitro validation; four of them are associated with traits and diseases that impact cardiovascular health. The impact of these variants on NKX2-5 binding was evaluated with electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) using recombinantly expressed and purified human NKX2-5 homeodomain. Binding curves were constructed to determine changes in binding between variant and reference alleles. Variants rs7350789, rs7719885, rs747334, and rs3892630 increased binding affinity, whereas rs61216514 decreased binding by NKX2-5 when compared to the reference genome. Our findings suggest that differential TF-DNA binding affinity can be key in establishing a causal mechanism of pathogenic variants. Abstract Figure
abstract_zh: 1. 摘要 全基因组关联研究（GWAS）已将超过90%的疾病或性状相关变异定位在非编码基因组中，例如顺式调控元件（cis-regulatory elements, CREs）。非编码单核苷酸多态性（SNPs）是基因组变异，可改变DNA结合调控蛋白（如转录因子（transcription factors, TFs））与基因组相互作用并调控基因表达的方式。NKX2-5是对心脏正常发育至关重要的转录因子，影响其功能的突变与先天性心脏病（congenital heart diseases, CHDs）相关。然而，建立非编码基因组变异与人类疾病之间的因果机制仍具挑战性。为应对这一挑战，我们使用基于位置权重矩阵（position weight matrix, PWM）的预测模型，识别出8,475个预测会改变NKX2-5 DNA结合的SNP。五个变异被优先用于体外验证；其中四个与影响心血管健康的性状和疾病相关。这些变异对NKX2-5结合的影响通过电泳迁移率变动分析（electrophoretic mobility shift assay, EMSA）评估，使用重组表达并纯化的人NKX2-5同源结构域。构建结合曲线以确定变异等位基因与参考等位基因之间的结合变化。与参考基因组相比，变异rs7350789、rs7719885、rs747334和rs3892630增加了结合亲和力，而rs61216514降低了NKX2-5的结合。我们的发现表明，差异性的TF-DNA结合亲和力可能是建立致病变异因果机制的关键。摘要图
